newsitem.title: JAPAN: DirecTV to enter Japan digital satellite market.
newsitem.headline: DirecTV to enter Japan digital satellite market.

text.p: Japan's TV viewers may be able to choose from more than 300 satellite broadcasting channels next year as DirecTV, a unit of Hughes Electronics, makes its debut to come head-to-head with two rival broadcasters.
DirecTV Japan Inc. said Tuesday that it would launch a 100-channel digital satellite broadcasting service in Japan in the autumn of 1997.

The new company will be battling for viewers against the 150-channel J-SkyB -- a venture between Australian media tycoon Rupert Murdoch's News Corp. Ltd. and Japan's Softbank Corp. J-SkyB will start its service next April.
Its other rival PerfecTV, a venture led by a consortium of leading Japanese trading houses, launched its service earlier this month.

DirecTV, for its part, brings together some household names. Japanese electronics giant Matsushita Electric Industrial Co. Ltd., the powerful Mitsubishi conglomerate and Hughes Electronics Corp. all have stakes in the venture.
DirecTV's entry will exacerbate the broadcasters' race to woo subscribers away from each other.
Hughes said the company needs to acquire three million subscribers to yield profits.

Prosperity in digital satellite broadcasting services is also expected to pose a threat to Japan's terrestrial broadcasters, who are protected by a government licensing system and currently immune to competition.
Michael Armstrong, chairman of Hughes Electronics, said on Tuesday that DirecTV would differentiate itself from other services by offering a higher quality service and competitive pricing.
"We have experience in the United States," he told a news conference. "We came to the U.S. market second...and today we have two million subscribers."
A spokeswoman for PerfecTV said the company has acquired 34,000 subscribers in the past two weeks alone.
Hughes is a subsidiary of General Motors Corp. that makes electronics, weapons and auto parts.
